subject: Compass update: quick market scan — model shifts & revenue risk
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.dev>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.dev, karthik.iyer@redwood.dev, marissa.cole@redwood.dev, jordan.blake@redwood.dev
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.dev
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Compass update: quick market scan — model shifts & revenue risk

Folks,

Quick heads-up ahead of the afternoon leadership sync and QBR slide refresh. Did a fast pass across the usual suspects and flagged three items that change our near-term risk profile for Hosted/Dedicated bookings:

- Argos AI: public release note this morning for Argos-70Q (70B quantized variant). They list a 2–3x cheaper token price on hosted latency-optimized endpoints vs prior gen; early benchmarks claim comparable ROUGE/BLEU on our internal eval slices. Samir (cc'd on this thread) shared the release notes — see attached.

- Nimbus Cloud: announced a "Real-Time Burst" pricing pilot in US-west that effectively undercuts our standard burst tier by ~30% for short-lived spikes. This is targeted at fintech partners and could affect some of our mid-market renewals.

- Helix Labs: quietly published a private deploy appliance for regulated customers (on-prem container image + managed control plane). This is a direct play on the same enterprise demand we're seeing for Private.

Immediate asks:
1) Laura: can you slot a 1-slide "revenue risk" callout into the QBR (data: impacted ARR, top-5 at-risk deals)? I included a stub slide in the Drive link.
2) Karthik: can Product/Applied ML run a fast eval (48–72h) comparing Argos-70Q on our prompt eval set (chat + codegen) and share perf/quality delta and cost implications? Priorities: latency tail, hallucination patterns, and safety regression risk.
3) Marissa & Jordan (Sales): update deal playbooks for AtlasCloud and any in-pipeline accounts flagged for pricing pressure — capture mitigation (discount guardrails, Dedicated commitments, contractual SLA options).

Attachments: compass_summary.pdf (summary + bullets), argos-70q-release-notes.txt (vendor release note).

I'm putting this on the top of the agenda for today's leadership 11:00 PT sync. Quick reactions welcome — otherwise we'll surface recommendations and proposed OKR adjustments in the meeting.

-Markus

--
Markus Klein
VP, Strategy & GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.dev>
To: markus.klein@redwood.dev
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.dev, marissa.cole@redwood.dev, jordan.blake@redwood.dev
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compass update: quick market scan — model shifts & revenue risk

Thanks Markus — good summary. I'll take the slide and add a short table: 
- Estimated ARR exposure (mid / high scenarios)
- Top 5 at-risk deals (with reason: pricing / model parity / on-prem need)
- Proposed mitigations (pricing corridors, Dedicated offers, short-term credits)

I'll pull AtlasCloud details from the CRM and upload the QBR slide by 10:30 so you can review before 11.

On the Argos-70Q note: Samir's release mentions quantization at 4-bit + new kernel tuning; that explains a lot of the cost delta. We should map their claimed latency numbers to our tail-latency SLOs before we panic — many of these claims don't hold under chat-style long-turn usage.

Laura

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.dev>
To: markus.klein@redwood.dev, laura.bennett@redwood.dev
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.dev, jordan.blake@redwood.dev
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compass update: quick market scan — model shifts & revenue risk

Adding some quick notes from Product/Applied ML POV:

- I'll spin up a narrow eval job today targeting our 10 representative prompts (3 chat flow, 4 codegen, 3 retrieval-augmented tasks). If we can get a small Argos-70Q endpoint (Samir, can you share a test key / endpoint?), we should be able to produce a perf + quality delta by EOD Thursday.
- Key metrics I'll surface: token-cost normalized CPU/GPU time, 95/99 latency tails for chat-style sessions, and a small battery of hallucination safety tests we've used in the last two quarters.
- If Argos is indeed 4-bit quant + new kernels, we need to watch cache behavior and long-turn memory — quantized kernels sometimes degrade KV cache efficiency which hits latency.

OKR implication suggestion: add a one-off "Competitive baseline" deliverable to the Serving OKR for this sprint (target: bench Argos vs our release candidate and publish guidance). We can scope down if the eval shows low risk.

-Karthik

Copy — we will:
- Update the AtlasCloud mutual action plan and push the Dedicated offering plus a short-term pricing protection clause into the playbook. I'll reach out to Ellen at AtlasCloud (procurement@atlascloud.com) to signal we're preparing options.
- Flag two in-pipeline renewals (ACCT-7782, ACCT-7890) for pricing-watch; I'll add recommended guardrails (max discount, term extension incentives).
- Prep a one-pager for sales that explains where Redwood still holds advantage (multi-deployment support, deterministic latency with SLOs, quality regressions protections via Optimize). Keep it <1 page.

I'll upload the updated playbook and the one-pager to the Drive folder by 16:00 PT.

-Marissa
